subject: Clarify: partial prefix / KV-cache hits — how are we billing token counts?
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@zephyrhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on prefix/KV cache billing (examples requested)

Thanks Aditya — quick question from our infra team as we prepare the SOW: when a request hits prefix/KV cache, what exactly are we billed for? We have three concrete cases and would appreciate line-item token math: 1) exact prefix match (client sends full 300-token prefix + prompt); 2) partial prefix match where only last 120 tokens match the cached key; 3) multi-turn session using KV cache where earlier turns are cached but response generation still consumes model compute. Also: do cache hits still consume request-token billing if the user-supplied prompt is identical? We need this to model month 1 usage.

Sam
Platform Engineer, Zephyr Health

High-level answers up front: Redwood bills for tokens consumed by the request and response as defined on the rate card, but there are special behaviors for prefix/KV cache hits that can change what we charge for the model compute portion. From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@zephyrhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, procurement@zephyrhealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on prefix/KV cache billing (examples requested)

Hi Sam — good questions. Below are concrete examples and the billing treatment per our hosted API rate card. I include assumptions at the top and then line-by-line math for each scenario.

Assumptions:
- Rate card: request tokens billed at $0.00001 / token, response tokens billed at $0.00002 / token (example entry-level hosted rate).
- Cache behavior: prefix/KV cache stores tokenized prefix->KV snapshot. On a cache hit, the model can avoid recomputing the prefix; however we still account for network/request transfer and may bill request-side tokens differently depending on hit type (see cases).
- For simplicity, 'request tokens' = tokens sent in prompt; 'response tokens' = tokens generated by model to complete the request.

Case A — Exact prefix match
Scenario: Client sends 300-token prefix + 50-token user prompt. The prefix key matches a cached KV snapshot exactly, so the serving runtime reuses KV cache and only generates the response based on the 50-token prompt + cached state.
Token math:
- Request tokens transmitted: 350 tokens (300 prefix + 50 prompt) — billed? Yes, per-token request charge applies on the wire (we charge incoming tokens). However, because the prefix is a cache hit, we apply a prefix-hit discount to the model compute portion.
- Model compute billed: only the compute to handle the 50-token prompt and generate the response; prefix compute avoided. On the rate card this is represented as 'response-side compute + request compute for non-cached tokens'. Practically, we bill request tokens at normal request rate but compute charge prorated to the effective tokens that required compute.
Example numbers (rounding):
- Request token charge: 350 * $0.00001 = $0.00350
- Compute/response charge (billed on effective compute tokens): assume 50 (prompt) + 200 (response) = 250 effective compute tokens * $0.00002 = $0.00500
- Total = $0.00850
Note: Because the 300-token prefix didn't cause model compute, we don't charge for the prefix compute portion — only the request transfer.

Case B — Partial prefix match (120-token suffix match)
Scenario: Client sends a 300-token prefix, but only 120 tokens at the end match an existing cached key. The runtime stitches the cached KV for the matched portion and recomputes the missing prefix tokens to reconstruct context before generating.
Token math:
- Request tokens transmitted: 350 tokens (billed at request rate) = 350 * $0.00001 = $0.00350
- Compute: because 120 tokens were cached, the runtime still needs to re-run 180 tokens worth of prefix tokens to reconstruct the full context plus prompt/response compute. So compute tokens = 180 (recomputed prefix) + 50 (prompt) + 200 (assumed response) = 430 tokens * $0.00002 = $0.00860
- Total = $0.01210

Case C — Multi-turn session (KV cache across turns)
Scenario: Multi-turn chat where early turns are cached server-side. On subsequent turns, the client sends a short 20-token prompt, but server-side KV contains representation of prior 6 turns.
Token math:
- Request tokens transmitted: 20 tokens * $0.00001 = $0.00020
- Compute: If the KV snapshot fully captures prior context, compute is only for the new prompt + response = 20 + 150 (response) = 170 tokens * $0.00002 = $0.00340
- Total = $0.00360

Other considerations / nuance:
- Network/request transfer: we bill tokens sent over the wire. If the client is sending the full prefix every time (even when cached server-side), those tokens are billable as request tokens. We can support an alternative API pattern where clients send a short reference id for server-held KV to avoid paying request-side token charges; this is available for Dedicated/Private customers and as a contractual addon for hosted customers (we can include as part of the SOW).
- Warm-cache credits: for ramp/initialization we can offer time-limited warm-cache credits (one-time credit bucket) so early prefix-heavy traffic does not spike month-1 bill. Laura will propose an amount based on forecast.
- Eviction/consistency: if the KV is evicted and recomputed, that request will incur full compute on the recompute call.

Let me know if you want these examples stuffed into a CSV for your cost model (I attached a sample CSV).

-Rishi
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on prefix/KV cache billing (examples requested)

Sam — following Rishi's breakdown, two commercial items to call out for the SOW:
1) "KV reference token" option: retain server-side KV keyed by an opaque id; the client can send the id instead of the full prefix to avoid request-token charges. This is a paid feature in hosted (add-on) and included for Redwood Dedicated. We propose including it in your SOW for the first 6 months as an onboarding credit.
2) Warm-cache credit: we can offer a $5k warm-cache credit applied as a discount to month 1 billing, specifically for prefix compute savings while your traffic patterns stabilize. If you accept the credit we will include explicit examples in the SOW showing the applied discount and the conditions (e.g., credit applies to billed compute-only amounts from cache-avoided tokens).

Proposed contract language (single sentence you can use in SOW):
"Redwood will apply server-side KV referencing for Zephyr Health as an add-on per the SOW. When Zephyr elects to use KV referencing, incoming request tokens will be billed only for tokens transmitted over the wire; model compute charges will be prorated to exclude compute saved by exact KV prefix hits, as illustrated in Appendix A (billing examples)."

We have attached a small CSV with the example rows to plug into your cost model. If you want, we can convert the CSV to a simple per-month estimate using your forecast.

Thanks — Laura
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Sam
